title: Supervised Training Rapidly Degrades Early Visual Cortex Alignment Across Biologically Plausible Learning Rules
abstract: arXiv:2605.30556v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: CORRECTION (August 2026): the central finding of this paper is not supported. An evaluation-mode defect left the batch-normalisation layers of the predictive-coding and STDP conditions in training mode during feature extraction, producing their apparent preservation of V1 alignment. With the defect repaired, predictive coding degrades V1 alignment more than backpropagation does, not less. The finding that training degrades V1 alignment for every rule tested does survive. See the correction note on page 1; the original abstract below and the body are unchanged from v1. Corrected analysis: arXiv:2608.12408. translated_title: 监督训练在生物合理学习规则下迅速降低早期视觉皮层对齐度
translated_abstract: arXiv:2605.30556v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：更正（2026年8月）：本文的核心发现不被支持。评估模式缺陷导致预测编码和STDP条件下的批归一化层在特征提取期间处于训练模式，从而产生了它们保留V1对齐的表象。修复该缺陷后，预测编码对V1对齐的退化程度大于反向传播，而非小于。训练对所有测试规则均降低V1对齐的发现仍然成立。详见第1页更正说明；以下原始摘要和正文与v1版本一致。更正分析：arXiv:2608.12408。随机、未训练的网络在早期视觉皮层的表征相似性上始终匹配或超过训练过的网络。这一令人困惑的发现挑战了学习改善大脑对齐的假设。我们通过追踪表征相似性分析（RSA）与人类fMRI数据的对齐来研究这一现象。
tldr: 该论文发现，监督训练在所有测试的生物合理学习规则下都会降低早期视觉皮层（V1）的表征对齐度，且随机未训练网络反而匹配或超越训练网络，挑战了学习改善大脑对齐的传统假设。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that supervised training degrades early visual cortex (V1) alignment under all tested biologically plausible learning rules, with random untrained networks matching or exceeding trained ones, challenging the assumption that learning improves brain alignment.
